title: On-device first-class client via PRIVATE FORK of Bitwarden SDK (DEFERRED)
description:
DEFERRED / backlog. Revive ONLY if the companion-push concept validates and on-device decrypt is still wanted. Direction: PRIVATE fork (NOT upstream) -- rationale (Andreas, 2026-08-11): side project; feature-flag swaps for embedded impls likely never ship in production, so it should not add cost to Bitwarden's real SDK.

Requires solving THREE independent fronts (per spike ai-bitwarden-hw-key-8d7.2):
1. SDK non-modularity + transport: fork bitwarden-api-base/-core/-key-connector to inject an esp-idf/mbedtls transport (no seam today; they use reqwest::Client directly). Also feature-gate bitwarden-api-key-connector out of bitwarden-crypto so 'just the KDF' is depend-able.
2. ring-on-xtensa (NOT fixed by forking BW crates): ring's bundled C crypto links wrong-endian on xtensa-esp32s3-espidf (build.rs target detection). Options: patch ring's build.rs, or swap rustls to a pure-Rust RustCrypto crypto provider to drop ring (unverified on xtensa).
3. On-hardware validation: footprint (512KB SRAM / 8MB PSRAM), real PBKDF2/Argon2id latency, session-key fast path -- ALL still unmeasured (no physical board during the spike).

Reference artifact: throwaway spike branch 'bd-ai-bitwarden-hw-key-8d7.2' (pushed to origin) contains spike-sdk/ with the minimal repro + exact mitigations (ring 'less-safe-getrandom-espidf' feature; opt-level=0 for rustls/mockall). DO NOT delete that branch.

title: M0: Platform Migration (T-Embed color + rotary, hardware-portable foundation)
description:
Green-field rebuild of the UI framework + app architecture for the Lilygo T-Embed (ESP32-S3, 320x170 color ST7789, rotary encoder), hardware-portable, first-class-Bitwarden-client direction. Synthesizes Ada's architecture design and Fern's UI-framework design.

KEY DECISIONS (orchestrator-reconciled from Ada + Fern):
- Platform-free 'core' crate; hardware injected behind a Platform boundary (Display/Input/Clock/Storage).
- Single generic main loop replaces the two divergent loops (main.rs vs bin/desktop.rs).
- Shared in-RAM Rgb565 framebuffer is the single render output; 3 run modes differ only at final flush -> headless screenshot faithful to device by construction.
- Rgb565 canonical throughout core (RESOLVED conflict: Ada proposed RGB888; Fern's Rgb565 wins for 3-mode fidelity). Core bound to Error=Infallible; mipidsi error absorbed at device surface.
- Retire BOTH GUI engines: src/gui/ is dead code (all call sites commented out); src/simple_gui/ custom RGBA rasterizer blocks color. Salvage concepts only (nav stack, ComponentAction, FocusEvent) reimplemented on embedded-graphics.
- Rotary-encoder NavIntent vocabulary (Next/Prev/NextN/Activate/Back) replaces 3-button KeyCode. Encoder-only for the M0 shell; keep intent seam for future button driver.
- SyncSource seam decouples app from the SDK spike; PushSyncSource (existing HTTP+CBOR) is fallback/dev aid, SdkSyncSource behind the spike.
- OSS: adopt embedded-graphics + embedded-graphics-framebuf + mipidsi + u8g2-fonts + light embedded-layout; defer embedded-menu to M1; reject slint/lvgl and SDL2 simulator.

DONE WHEN (roadmap.md M0): empty-but-real 320x170 color shell, encoder-drivable, running identically in all three modes (headless/windowed/real-target); SDK spike delivers a go/no-go + ADR.

title: W1: Freeze core interfaces (Platform/Surface/Framebuffer/InputEvent/Clock/Storage) + NavIntent + record ADRs
description: Joint Ada+Fern interface freeze -> ADR-ready. Freeze: Framebuffer (in-RAM Rgb565, embedded-graphics-framebuf), DisplaySurface (flushes framebuffer; Error=Infallible in core, mipidsi error at device adapter), InputSource + rotary InputEvent, NavIntent enum {Next,Prev,NextN(u16),Activate,Back}, Clock, Storage (opaque-blob KV), Platform capability bundle, SyncSource seam. Gates almost everything. Output: ADRs (surface/run-mode seam; portability+workspace; input model; sync-source seam; UI-framework reuse-vs-rewrite) + updated INDEX/progress/roadmap.

title: W8: SDK feasibility spike (throwaway) — build/link, footprint, KDF latency, session-key fast path
description: PARALLEL, START NOW, gates M1 sync DIRECTION not the M0 shell. Throwaway spike bin/branch. Prove: (1) Bitwarden Rust SDK dep tree builds/links for xtensa-esp32s3-espidf — top unknown is TLS (rustls/ring vs esp-idf mbedtls) and async runtime (tokio on esp-idf); (2) footprint fits ~512KB SRAM + 8MB PSRAM; (3) KDF/unlock latency measured on-device (PBKDF2 600k, Argon2id) — the UX gate; (4) session-key fast-path prototype (full unlock once -> wrap+persist session key -> re-unlock cheap). Output: go/no-go + measurements + ADR. NOT merged firmware.

comments.author: Andreas Coroiu
comments.text:
PROGRESS 1/3: Set up spike-sdk/ (throwaway, xtensa-esp32s3-espidf, ESP-IDF v5.3.3, reusing existing .embuild toolchain via symlink to dodge a Zscaler TLS-interception issue with Python's cert store that blocked fresh esp-idf tool installs).

FINDING A (ring/rustls, real bug + real fix): Just adding bitwarden-crypto as a dependency (no networking touched directly) transitively pulls in reqwest+rustls+ring via bitwarden-crypto -> bitwarden-api-key-connector. Initial build failed: ring 0.17.14's SystemRandom does not implement rustls's required SecureRandom trait on this target -> 9 compile errors in rustls-0.23.43/src/crypto/ring/*.rs (e.g. 'the trait bound SystemRandom: ring::rand::sealed::SecureRandom is not satisfied'). Root cause confirmed by reading ring-0.17.14/src/rand.rs: target_os=espidf IS supported by ring, but only behind ring's own opt-in feature 'less-safe-getrandom-espidf' (ring/src/rand.rs:126), which is NOT enabled by default when rustls pulls ring in transitively. FIX: adding an explicit 'ring = { version = "0.17", features = ["less-safe-getrandom-espidf"] }' to Cargo.toml forces the feature on via Cargo feature unification (ring is a single shared dependency in the graph) -> ring+rustls then compile cleanly for xtensa-esp32s3-espidf. So: ring/rustls CAN be made to build on esp-idf, it just needs this one non-obvious feature flag. Good news for the TLS sub-question.

FINDING B (new blocker, unrelated to TLS): after fixing ring, build now fails on mockall v0.15.0 with an opaque 'error: Undefined temporary symbol' (LLVM/assembler-level error, no source location) when rustc targets xtensa-esp32s3-espidf. Confirmed via 'cargo tree -i mockall': mockall is pulled in by bitwarden-api-key-connector (crates/bitwarden-api-key-connector/Cargo.toml) as an UNCONDITIONAL, non-optional, non-dev dependency (not feature gated). bitwarden-api-key-connector is itself an unconditional dependency of bitwarden-crypto. So there is no way to depend on 'just bitwarden-crypto' (KDF/crypto primitives) without also pulling in mockall, reqwest, reqwest-middleware, and tokio (full/default features) -- the entire HTTP/API-client stack rides along even when you only want the crypto primitives. mockall itself then hits what looks like an xtensa-LLVM backend codegen bug (reproduced in isolation via 'cargo build -p mockall --target xtensa-esp32s3-espidf', same error in both debug and release profiles). This blocks forward progress on footprint/KDF/session-key measurements via the real bitwarden-crypto crate as currently structured.

comments.author: Andreas Coroiu
comments.text:
PROGRESS 2/3: Isolated the TLS stack (reqwest+rustls+rustls-platform-verifier+tokio) from the mockall blocker by temporarily dropping bitwarden-crypto from Cargo.toml. rustls itself (independent of bitwarden, independent of mockall) hit the SAME 'error: Undefined temporary symbol' xtensa-LLVM codegen bug found in mockall -- confirmed via 'cargo build -p rustls --release -v' targeting xtensa-esp32s3-espidf. WORKAROUND FOUND: adding '[profile.release.package.rustls] opt-level = 0' (and same for mockall) avoids the bug -- this looks like an xtensa-LLVM backend optimizer bug, not something either crate does wrong. Re-enabled bitwarden-crypto with both mitigations (ring/less-safe-getrandom-espidf feature + opt-level=0 overrides for rustls+mockall) and got PAST compilation for the first time, all the way to the final link step.

FINDING C (the decisive blocker, exactly the risk flagged in the bead): the combined image fails at LINK time with a genuine ring bug: 'ld: ...libring-*.rlib(a0330e891e733f4e-gfp_p384.o): compiled for a big endian system and target is little endian' / 'ld: cross-endian linking for ...(curve25519.o) not supported', repeated across gfp_p384.o, p256.o, limbs.o, mem.o, poly1305.o, ecp_nistz.o, curve25519.o. Root cause: ring's build.rs compiles its bundled C crypto sources via the 'cc' crate, and its target-arch detection does not have a correct entry for xtensa-esp32s3-espidf, so it ends up invoking the xtensa-esp-elf-gcc cross-compiler with the wrong endianness assumption for at least some of its C translation units, producing object files that cannot be linked against the rest of the (correctly little-endian) xtensa binary. This is a ring-crate limitation (ring has never had official xtensa support), not something fixable from the SDK or app side without patching ring's own build.rs. Confirms the bead's top hypothesis: 'ring's per-arch assembly likely won't build for xtensa' -- it manifests as a cross-endian C-object link failure rather than a missing-assembly-file error, but the practical result is identical: ring cannot be linked for this target as currently pulled in by the SDK.

Compounding structural finding: bitwarden-crypto (meant to be 'just the crypto/KDF primitives') has an UNCONDITIONAL, non-optional dependency on bitwarden-api-key-connector (crates/bitwarden-api-key-connector/Cargo.toml), which itself unconditionally depends on mockall + reqwest + reqwest-middleware + tokio. There is no Cargo feature to opt out. So you cannot depend on 'just the KDF' from this SDK without also pulling in, and successfully linking, its full HTTP/TLS/mocking stack. And bitwarden-api-base (crates/bitwarden-api-base/Cargo.toml) hard-wires reqwest+rustls+rustls-platform-verifier for all non-wasm targets with no seam to substitute a different HTTP/TLS client -- routing through esp-idf/mbedtls instead of rustls would require forking bitwarden-api-base (and likely bitwarden-core, bitwarden-api-api, bitwarden-api-identity, bitwarden-api-key-connector) since they use reqwest::Client directly, not behind a trait.

CAVEAT (environment): no physical T-Embed / ESP32-S3 hardware is attached to this dev machine (checked /dev/tty.*, /dev/cu.*, USB device list -- none found). Even where compilation succeeded, no on-device flashing/timing/footprint measurement was possible. Real link/footprint/KDF-latency numbers require someone with the physical board. For rough context only (NOT representative of ESP32-S3 Xtensa LX7 @ 240MHz + PSRAM), I ran the exact pinned KDF crate versions bitwarden-crypto uses (pbkdf2 0.13.0-rc.10, argon2 0.6.0-rc.8) on the host dev machine: PBKDF2-SHA256 600k iters = 41.9ms, Argon2id 64MiB/3-iter/4-lane (Bitwarden's default client KDF params) = 87.2ms, both on host CPU (Apple Silicon class), not ESP32-S3. Host-to-embedded scaling for this workload is commonly 1-2 orders of magnitude slower on Xtensa LX7 for the PBKDF2/SHA2 hashing itself, and Argon2id's 64MiB working set would have to live in PSRAM (SPI-attached, far lower bandwidth than internal SRAM), which is likely to dominate its cost beyond simple clock-scaling -- this is a hypothesis, not a measurement.

comments.author: Andreas Coroiu
comments.text:
GO/NO-GO RECOMMENDATION (evidence-based, see PROGRESS 1-2 comments for full detail and exact error text):

NO-GO on 'SDK does its own on-device TLS/HTTP directly (reqwest+rustls) for sync', as currently structured, for xtensa-esp32s3-espidf. Evidence: reproducible LINK failure -- ring's bundled C crypto objects (gfp_p384.o, p256.o, curve25519.o, poly1305.o, ecp_nistz.o, mem.o, limbs.o) compile with the wrong endianness for this target and fail to link ('cross-endian linking...not supported'). This is a ring build.rs/target-detection limitation with no known app-side fix, compounded by an xtensa-LLVM optimizer bug that separately breaks rustls/mockall at nonzero opt-levels (workaroundable, but signals xtensa Rust toolchain immaturity for this class of dependency). Additionally, bitwarden-crypto cannot be depended on in isolation -- it unconditionally pulls the same broken reqwest/rustls/ring stack (plus mockall) via bitwarden-api-key-connector, so even 'just use the SDK's crypto/KDF, roll your own transport' is not possible without a fork.

The only path to make the real Bitwarden Rust SDK work on this hardware would be forking bitwarden-api-base/-core/-api/-identity/-key-connector to replace reqwest+rustls with an esp-idf/mbedtls-backed HTTP client (no existing seam for this) AND getting a working ring replacement or patching ring's build.rs for xtensa -- both are non-trivial, ongoing-maintenance forks of Bitwarden's own 'internal, do not use' crates, not a build-flag change.

RECOMMENDATION: for M1, do NOT plan on-device SDK-driven sync/decrypt via the real bitwarden-crypto/bitwarden-core crates as currently published. The push-fallback direction (server/companion pushes already-decrypted or device-specific-encrypted data to the device, device does no TLS/HTTP/full-SDK work) remains the only demonstrated-feasible sync direction from this spike. If on-device SDK sync is still wanted long-term, treat it as a much larger, separate initiative: (a) fork+maintain patched bitwarden-api-base with a custom transport, (b) get ring (or an alternative RustCrypto-only rustls provider, if one exists) working on xtensa, (c) revisit only after both are proven in isolation.

NOT ANSWERED (blocked by the above + no physical hardware attached to this dev machine): footprint fit in 512KB SRAM/8MB PSRAM, real on-device PBKDF2/Argon2id latency, session-key fast-path prototype/timing. These all require a working link (not achieved) and/or a flashed device (none available here). Host-CPU-only reference numbers for the two KDFs are in the prior comment, explicitly flagged as non-representative.

Spike branch (throwaway, not for merge): bd-ai-bitwarden-hw-key-8d7.2, pushed to origin. spike-sdk/ contains the minimal repro (Cargo.toml shows the exact ring feature + opt-level mitigations; Cargo.lock pins the exact bitwarden-crypto git rev and dependency versions used).

title: W2: Workspace restructure — extract platform-free 'core' crate; migrate credential model to VaultItem
description: Split single crate into workspace: core (lib, no platform deps), firmware (esp bin), emulator (host bin). Makes the portable-core boundary compiler-enforced instead of convention (today core can 'use esp_idf_svc' and only fail on host build). Migrate src/credentials/mod.rs into core as a VaultItem view-model (projection from any SyncSource), decoupled from push-CBOR Credential and SDK Cipher.

comments.author: Andreas Coroiu
comments.text:
APPROACH: Converted single crate to a 3-member workspace (core/firmware/emulator) per the ADR. Structural calls made beyond the literal ADR text:
1. core package named 'bhk-core' (not literally 'core') to avoid crate-name collision with the sysroot 'core' crate under an --extern path dependency; directory is still core/ per the ADR.
2. The old GUI engines (gui/, simple_gui/) are duplicated between firmware/ and emulator/ rather than centralized, since both binaries need them and the bead explicitly forbids putting them in bhk-core. Pruned emulator's copy of gui/ down to just the input submodule (InputInterface/KeyCode/InputEvent) since emulator never uses the rest of the old engine (document/layout/render/style/primitives/icons) -- only firmware's view.rs exercises the full old engine. simple_gui/ + simple_view.rs are duplicated in full (both bins use them).
3. firmware no longer carries the wire-format credentials module at all (dropped entirely) -- nothing in firmware ever consumed Credential/SyncRequest/SyncResponse. That wire format now lives only in emulator/src/credentials/mod.rs, with new From<Credential>/From<&Credential> impls converting to bhk_core::VaultItem at the HTTP/storage boundary (emulator/src/main.rs).
4. core::input::NavIntent, core::platform::{DisplaySurface,InputSource,Clock,Storage,FrameBuffer565}, core::sync_source::{SyncSource,UnlockToken} added as placeholder/trait-only seams per the ADRs -- no implementations, no SdkSyncSource (per instructions).

comments.author: Andreas Coroiu
comments.text: LEARNED: On this machine, a fresh worktree triggers esp-idf-sys's first-time network bootstrap (git clone of esp-idf + python venv + constraints-file download), which hit two environment issues unrelated to the code: a transient GitHub 502 on submodule fetch (retry fixed it), and a Python (pyenv 3.13.9) SSL CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED on the constraints download that 'pip install certifi' + SSL_CERT_FILE did NOT fix (the idf_tools.py venv's urllib doesn't pick it up). Worked around by symlinking .worktrees/.../\.embuild -> the main checkout's already-bootstrapped .embuild (gitignored either way, so this is a pure local dev convenience, not part of the shipped change). Future agents hitting the same SSL error on a fresh worktree should look for an existing .embuild in a sibling checkout before debugging Python cert config from scratch.

comments.author: Andreas Coroiu
comments.text: Completed: split single crate into a 3-member Cargo workspace (core=bhk-core, firmware, emulator) per the portability-boundary ADR. VaultItem view-model migrated to core with placeholder DisplaySurface/InputSource/Clock/Storage/SyncSource/NavIntent seams (no impls, no SdkSyncSource). Old gui/simple_gui engines preserved, duplicated across firmware+emulator (pruned to input-only in emulator's gui/ copy since only firmware's view.rs uses the full old engine). Both cargo build -p firmware (xtensa, sourced export-esp.sh) and cargo build --bin desktop --target aarch64-apple-darwin (host) build and link successfully; the json_to_cbor example was smoke-tested end to end.

title: W3: Render core + UI framework on embedded-graphics (Rgb565 framebuffer, Widget/Action/FocusEvent, nav stack)
description: Fern's core deliverable. Retire src/gui/ (dead) + src/simple_gui/ RGBA rasterizer. Reimplement on embedded-graphics + embedded-graphics-framebuf: retained-mode Widget trait {measure, render(area, &mut Surface), is_focusable, on_focus, on_intent}; Action = PushView/PopView/Back/None; Navigator owns screen stack (salvage simple_gui/document nav-stack + focus memory); region layout (title/content/hint bars) + linear stacks, light embedded-layout; true clipping via DrawTargetExt::clipped() (retire char-skip marquee); u8g2-fonts foreground-colored text (retire baked leaked mono fonts + '?'-fallback bug). Depends on W1 interface freeze; UI-framework reuse-vs-rewrite ADR is part of W1.

title: W9: SyncSource trait + PushSyncSource (wrap existing HTTP+CBOR push)
description: Introduce SyncSource {sync()->Vec<VaultItem>, unlock(secret)} so App never names the SDK or HTTP server directly. PushSyncSource wraps the demoted-but-working HTTP+CBOR push (src/desktop/http_server.rs, Arc<Mutex<Vec<Credential>>>). SdkSyncSource is developed behind W8. This is the decoupling that de-gates M0/M1 from the spike outcome.

title: W4: Host surface adapters — MinifbSurface, HeadlessSurface(PNG), host Clock, file Storage
description: Host adapters flushing the shared Rgb565 framebuffer. MinifbSurface: Rgb565->ARGB8888->minifb (from bin/desktop.rs). HeadlessSurface: keep last frame in RAM, PNG-encode on demand for screenshot capture, no window. Host Clock; file Storage (from src/desktop/storage.rs). One host binary, surface chosen at runtime (--headless flag) so both stay compiled and cannot drift; exact ergonomics are Tess's call.

title: W6: T-Embed board adapter — St7789Surface (mipidsi), rotary InputSource, esp Clock, NVS Storage, BoardConfig pin map
description: Real-target adapter. St7789Surface via mipidsi (add mipidsi + display-interface-spi; keep ssd1306 only until parity proven, then drop). Rotary-encoder driver producing NavIntent. esp Clock; NVS-backed Storage. BoardConfig pin map + peripheral init live ONLY here (today hardcoded in src/main.rs:47-115).

title: W5: Headless input-injection + screenshot protocol (extend http_server.rs)
description: Extend the existing SyncServer HTTP endpoints so the agent harness injects NavIntent (NOT raw hardware) and captures PNG screenshots from HeadlessSurface. Hardware-agnostic test path. Co-owned Ruby + Tess.

title: W7: Unified Platform-generic main loop; wire all three modes; delete old engines (closes M0)
description: Single run<P: Platform>() loop (input.poll -> app.handle_input -> app.step -> if dirty: display.present(app.render) -> clock.sleep). Wire headless/windowed/real-target. Build the region layout + scrolling-list widget (viewport auto-scroll, true clipping) = the empty-but-real encoder-drivable color shell. Delete src/gui/ + src/simple_gui/ at parity. This is M0 done-when.
